case: `grant_stripping_probe_result`'s owner is handed back to S1-C03 -- the producing executor whose grants the probe is about -- in BOTH places it is declared: the registry field and the pinned row.
why: F6D-05: the committed state the finding measured. The positive control on grant removal was a field on the record whose grants are being removed, and R-X15's own argument is that the rule must be structural rather than asserted. One word restores it, and nothing but this check notices. WRONG_REASON LEAK, FIXED IN THE SAME LANE THAT WROTE IT. The first version patched the REGISTRY ONLY, so the two declarations disagreed and the two-place guard fired first -- 'a producer-unauthorable field's owner differs from the pinned one' -- and the fixture was rejected without its own check ever running. A one-place mutation tests the mirror, not the rule; the rule is what a determined editor would do, which is edit both. Patching both puts A POSITIVE CONTROL IS OWNED BY THE PARTY IT CONTROLS in front of it, and the mirror keeps its own separate value: it is what makes the two-place edit visible, not what refuses it.
expect_failure_contains: A POSITIVE CONTROL IS OWNED BY THE PARTY IT CONTROLS
